reasoning_traces.think:
The core methodology employs a probabilistic simulation engine to evaluate draft strategies by modeling draft positions as normally distributed around ADP with standard deviation SD. Players are ranked by projected fantasy points (FPT) within each position group. The simulation iterates over 100 repetitions per year across 10 years, producing 2.016 million total draft picks. This approach enables comparison between standard drafting and zero-running back strategies by quantifying expected value under uncertainty. The framework assumes stable player performance and draft behavior, with failure modes including data staleness, non-normality of draft distributions, and misalignment between projected and actual FPT. The model's dual nature lies in its ability to simulate both individual pick outcomes and aggregate strategic effectiveness.
